subject: Sales discovery: model evals & multilingual quality (EU / APAC) - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aurelia Ramos <aurelia@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps: multilingual evals (EU / APAC)

Hi Aurelia —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Goals you shared: improve customer support responses in French/German (EU) and Japanese/Korean (APAC), keep latency under 300ms for chat flows, and maintain strict data residency for EU production.
- Current constraints: heavy peak-hour traffic in EU region, existing prompt set is English-first and shows quality drop when translated; procurement wants clear cost and timeline for a small PoC.

Recommended initial model candidates for the PoC (based on your quality/latency trade-offs):
1) redwood/m2-13b-multilang (13B) — best out-of-the-box multilingual quality for EU languages, slightly higher token cost but better few-shot generalization.
2) redwood/opt-7b-8k-quant (7B quantized) — lower cost + faster tail latency; good for lower-lift deployment as a backup variant.
3) redwood/verse-30b-eu (30B trimmed for EU locales) — if you want top-tier German/French quality for critical flows (budget permitting).

I attached a starter prompt set (globex_prompt_set_v1.txt) and our latest multilingual eval CSV (globex_multilingual_eval_results_20270419.csv) from the quick benchmark we ran after the call. The CSV highlights per-language F1 / human preference scores and token cost estimates at 512-token average.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You share 10–15 representative prompts per language (we can use the attached prompt set as a template).
- We run a two-week PoC focused on French/German + Japanese with both the 13B multilang and the 7B quantized model variants.
- Baseline quality/regression checks: we will run your prompts through current translations and compare to our candidate models; anything with >10-point delta in human preference we'll flag as a regression and propose mitigation (prompt engineering or switching variants).
- Outline mutual action plan and procurement asks (I attached a draft MAP).

Questions for you:
1) Can you confirm which EU country data must stay in-region (France/Germany only, or pan-EU)?
2) Who should be the technical contact for the PoC (we can loop in Jonas for an SRE kickoff)?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal resources once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: globex_prompt_set_v1.txt, globex_multilingual_eval_results_20270419.csv, Mutual-Action-Plan-Globex.docx

From: Aurelia Ramos <aurelia@globexretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Peter Tan <peter.tan@acmeasia.co>, Jiro Sato <jiro.sato@tokyoretail.jp>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps: multilingual evals (EU / APAC)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications before we move to the PoC: 

- Data residency: initially France and Germany only for the EU PoC. Production will likely be pan-EU but we need to validate with legal.
- Technical contact for PoC: Jiro Sato (engineering) for APAC, and Peter Tan will own integration in SE Asia. I'll be the project sponsor.
- Budget: procurement wants a rough cost delta between the 13B and 7B options for a 30-day active PoC (estimate tokens/day = 1.2M). Can you include cost examples?

Also — can you confirm whether Redwood can run the linguistic evals with native annotators (we can supplement with our ops team) and whether results will include per-language confusion matrices? That would help our product folks.

Happy to set a 30-minute sync with the engineering leads this week.

Best,
Aurelia
Head of AI Ops | Globex Retail
aurelia@globexretail.com

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aurelia Ramos <aurelia@globexretail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps: multilingual evals (EU / APAC)

Hi Aurelia — quick answers inline and some follow-up details.

> Data residency: initially France and Germany only for the EU PoC.
Yep — we can pin routing to EU regions only for the PoC. For production we support pan-EU deployment with customer-managed VPCs and KMS integration (cc Neha for SSO/KMS and audit-log details).

> Budget: procurement wants a rough cost delta between the 13B and 7B options for a 30-day active PoC (1.2M tokens/day).
Estimated unit cost (very approximate until we run with your real prompts):
- redwood/m2-13b-multilang: ~$0.0009 per token => ~1,080 / day => ~32,400 for 30 days.
- redwood/opt-7b-8k-quant: ~$0.00035 per token => ~420 / day => ~12,600 for 30 days.
We’ll provide line-item estimates once we run the 50-sample eval and see average output lengths.

> Native annotators and confusion matrices
We can run the initial pass with Redwood-managed linguists in FR/DE/JP/KO and provide per-language confusion matrices and error buckets. If Globex wants to supply internal annotators, we can incorporate their labels into the same evaluation pipeline.

Quality/regression guardrails (proposal):
- Baseline: run your current translated prompts through a reference (current system) and compute human preference / BLEU / intent F1.
- Candidate vs baseline: flag any prompt that drops >10 absolute points in human preference or increases hallucination rate above 5%.
- Canary approach: run 10% traffic to new variant for 48 hours, compare metrics; automatic fallback to the prior variant if key metrics regress.

Attachments & links: the CSV attached is the quick benchmark we discussed. Full benchmark with per-language confusion matrices is at: https://redwood-inference-benchmarks.internal/202704/globex_multilingual_report

Next actions I’ll take this week:
- Rishi will scope the PoC infra and produce a short runbook (cc'd).
- Jonas will reach out to schedule the technical kickoff and SRE checklist.
- I’ll share a refined MAP and a 10-sample, per-language submission template.

If that works, can you confirm Jiro + Peter as technical leads and approve the MAP?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments referenced: globex_multilingual_eval_results_20270419.csv, Mutual-Action-Plan-Globex.docx

Hi Aurelia / team —

Quick note from the SRE/solutions side: I can own the PoC kickoff. Proposed immediate milestones:
- Day 0–3: onboarding + sample prompt ingestion (we will validate format, run a smoke pass across both variants).
- Day 4–10: linguist annotation + automated metric pass (we will compute confusion matrices and preference scoring).
- Day 11–14: canary traffic run + cost/latency SLO check.

For the EU PoC we will provision capacity in Frankfurt and Paris zones only. For APAC we'll provision Tokyo and Singapore per your preference. We will also enable per-request region pinning, and we can export audit logs (Neha to confirm KMS/Azure GCP/HSM connectors).

Please pick two 30-minute slots for a technical kickoff (I included a Calendly link below) and drop the sample prompts in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cGP-Globex-Evals

Calendly: https://calendly.com/jonas-redwood/poc-kickoff-30m

Looking forward —
